## Summary

**Candidate submitted:** Rule `[33+, 35-]` — long feature 33, short feature 35, equal-weighted.

**In-sample performance:** Sharpe 0.491 (all years equal) / 0.554 (recent years weighted) — clearly ahead of the baseline model (0.183 / 0.246, turnover 0.042).

**Process:**
- Declared three stopping rules upfront (best-so-far stop at 1.0, failures-stop at 3, last-gain restart at 0.02) and a weak prior favoring parsimony (single feature, feature 0).
- `init` anchored on feature 32 instead, and across **six independent restarts** (anchors 32, 33, 18, 16, 19, 38), feature **35 (short)** repeatedly emerged as the best complementary partner — a reassuring sign of robustness rather than a one-off fluke.
- The peak combination found was `[33+, 35-]` at 0.491, consistently beating every other 2- and 3-feature combination tried, including attempts to extend to a third feature (which always degraded performance).
- I had to adjust my restart trigger mid-search when it became oversensitive (firing on nearly every move), which I logged transparently via `change_trigger`.
- A `pick` call was misapplied and drifted the "held" state away from the best rule, but the harness correctly tracked and submitted the **true best-found rule**, `[33+, 35-]`, when I called `submit_candidate`.

**Key caveat:** The gate's 90% lower bound came back at **L90 = -0.625**, a very wide and partly negative interval — a clear warning sign that despite the robustness evidence (same partner feature across many anchors), the in-sample Sharpe is likely inflated by search/selection effects. 

**Final prediction:** mean annualized net Sharpe **0.15**, standard deviation **0.45** — a substantial discount from the in-sample 0.49, reflecting genuine uncertainty about whether this edge survives out-of-sample.
